scenario.summary: SafePay ransomware actors gain initial access through credential harvesting, brute-force attacks, and exploitation of vulnerabilities in VPN and edge devices like Cisco and Veeam. Once inside, they escalate privileges via UAC bypass, move laterally using RDP and PsExec, and utilize RMM tools for persistence before exfiltrating data and deploying encryption.

meta.rationale: Prioritize servers hosting sensitive data, backup storage controllers, and administration workstations. SafePay typically inhibits recovery before the final encryption phase.
meta.hypothesis: Adversaries have staged data using rare archival or cloud-sync tools and are now inhibiting system recovery by deleting shadow copies before executing a ransomware payload that renames user files to include the .SafePay extension.

hunt.name: SafePay Ransomware: Exfiltration and Impact
hunt.description: SafePay ransomware, active since August 2024, follows a high-velocity chain from data collection to encryption. This hunt focuses on the high-impact finale: data exfiltration and the destructive impact phase. It identifies the use of archival and sync tools (RClone, FileZilla, B2) that are rare across the fleet—leveraging original filename metadata to catch renamed binaries—and correlates them with attempts to inhibit recovery by deleting shadow copies. Finally, it looks for the characteristic file renaming activity that appends the .SafePay extension. The hunt follows a funnel flow, using recovery inhibition as a scoping lead before fanning out to parallel behavioral and prevalence checks.

nodes.label: Lead: Shadow copy deletion and recovery inhibition

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE ((LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\vssadmin.exe' AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%delete%') OR (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\wbadmin.exe' AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%delete%')) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') ORDER BY device_hostname, time
config.description: Identify hosts where system recovery mechanisms are being disabled, a common precursor to ransomware encryption. Ordering by time and host allows the analyst to see the sequence of destructive commands.
config.expected_signal: Rows showing vssadmin or wbadmin being used to delete backup data, sequenced by host. This narrows the hunt to hosts at immediate risk of impact.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_name) AS tool_path, process_original_file_name, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, COUNT(*) AS runs, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{exfil_tools}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_original_file_name) || ',') > 0 OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\7z.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\winrar.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\rclone.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\filezilla.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\winscp.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\b2.exe') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY tool_path, process_original_file_name HAVING host_count <= 5 ORDER BY host_count, runs
config.description: Find tools like RClone or FileZilla using both robust basename matching and original filename metadata to detect renamed binaries. Stack-counting identifies which tools are rare and thus suspicious.
config.expected_signal: Execution of archival tools on five or fewer hosts. Matching against original filename catches cases where SafePay actors renamed RClone or FileZilla to evade filename filters.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_path, process_name, actor_user_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%.safepay' AND activity_id IN (1, 5) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Locate the primary indicator of encryption: the creation or renaming of files to the .SafePay extension. Including activity_id 5 catches mass renames typical of encryption.
config.expected_signal: A burst of file renames or creations with the .safepay extension. Zero results suggests the impact stage has not yet triggered or is not visible on enrolled hosts.

config.objective: Decide whether the evidence supports a diagnosis of SafePay ransomware activity, specifically identifying hosts where recovery inhibition (shadow deletion) or exfiltration tool usage preceded .SafePay file activity.
config.description: Synthesize the timeline from recovery inhibition to rare staging tools and finally to file encryption.
config.expected_signal: A detailed assessment per host citing the progression of malicious actions.
config.success_criteria: A verdict of malicious for hosts with .SafePay files or shadow copy deletions combined with rare archival tools.

config.description: Manually confirm the malicious nature of identified tools and assess the extent of file encryption.
config.instructions: Review the hosts flagged for rare tools and recovery inhibition. Cross-reference with authorized IT maintenance windows. If legitimate archival software is found, update the rare_exfiltration_tools parameter to exclude it.

config.description: Finalize the hunt and document findings.
config.instructions: Document all confirmed malicious activity. Record the time between exfiltration tool usage and encryption start to help tune future detection latency. Note any hosts that were scoped but lacked file telemetry.
